rationale: The noun zera ("seed") appears in 3:15 and again at 4:25, where Eve names Seth "another seed in place of Abel" after Cain kills Abel; what is traced is a recurring word doing narrative work, which is why the type is motif and not covenant_development. Collins (Tyndale Bulletin 48.1, 1997) and Alexander (Tyndale Bulletin 48.2, 1997) argue on syntactic grounds for a singular seed and for the same pattern in other Genesis seed statements. Cheek reports that Walton and Abernethy-Goswell dispute this and read the pattern as collective, so the label is strong, not explicit: the case rests on named scholarship with named dissent, not on a text that names its own connection.
